===== fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular.md
---
name: fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular
description: "fight-ai round \"ground truth\" spans are auto-seeded from the pipeline's own AI output, so scoring round IoU against them is circular"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 579b1254-323f-42d1-b482-42c5ad365f5c
---

`backend/app/services/label_span_service.py:10-34` seeds `label_spans` of kind
`round` from the `rounds` table (AI segmentation output) the first time the
Annotate page requests them, so the labeller starts pre-filled. If nobody edits
them, the "ground truth" is byte-identical to the prediction.

As of 2026-08-17 that was true of fight 46 (DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA) — 3 spans, one
shared microsecond-identical `created_at`, `labeled_at` NULL, 0 strike events,
and `segmentation_needs_review = true` with a reason calling the boundaries
"a guess". Fight 42 also matched AI output exactly; only fight 44 had a
human-adjusted round start.

**Why:** scoring round IoU against seeded spans reads 1.000 before any change
and makes every genuine segmentation *improvement* look like a regression.

**How to apply:** before trusting a round-IoU number, check whether the label
span differs from the `rounds` row and whether the span timestamps are
distinct. `eval.cli export` refuses fights with `labeled_at IS NULL`, which
catches the unfinished case but *not* the seeded-then-finished case.
Also note 3 of 4 fights were processed on the manual-labeling track and have
zero `fight_events`, so strike P/R/F1 is structurally 0 for them.
See [[easyocr-confidence-is-noise]].

===== corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground.md
---
name: corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground
description: "eval/corner_accuracy.py reads the shorts band as a fraction of bbox height, so it goes nearly blind on ground/clinch frames — a low decisive-frame count is \"unverified\", not \"fine\""
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 53047172-e54e-4eb1-a0f1-31064b2e9209
  modified: 2026-08-23T07:32:54.047Z
---

`ai/eval/corner_accuracy.py` samples each fighter's shorts band at
`_BAND_TOP=0.42` to `_BAND_BOTTOM=0.72` **of bbox height**. That geometry only
lands on the trunks when the fighter is upright. On the ground the bbox goes
wide-and-short and the band slices across arms, canvas and the opponent, so
`_colour_vote` almost never clears `_MIN_COLOUR_PX` / `_MIN_DECISIVENESS`.

Measured 2026-08-23 on DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA (a ground-heavy fight, 83 of 163 hand
labels are `ground_punch`), frames 1199–34767 at stride 15 (~2200 frames
sampled):

- fight 48 (old pipeline): **7** decisive frames
- fight 52 (new pipeline): **3** decisive frames

Whole-fight at stride 10 the same fight yields 55 decisive frames — i.e. the
evidence comes almost entirely from the standing portions elsewhere in the video.

**Why:** a whole-fight accuracy number is therefore not evenly distributed over
the fight. It can read "56% correct" while contributing essentially zero
evidence about the ground exchanges, which is exactly where tracker identity
swaps are most likely and where corner errors do the most damage to training
data.

**How to apply:** treat a low decisive-frame count as *unverified*, never as a
pass — the module's own docstring says this for the zero case and the same
applies at n=3. For ground-heavy footage, verify corners by eye
(`--verify-pose` overlay video) or via labeller-marked `corner_swap` spans
rather than trusting this number. Also note `format_accuracy` only prints runs
of >= 3 frames (`min_run`), so short flapping runs are invisible in its output —
count runs, not just accuracy, to see instability. Related:
[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]], [[fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan]].

===== easyocr-confidence-is-noise.md
---
name: easyocr-confidence-is-noise
description: "EasyOCR line confidence on fight-ai scoreboard crops is noise-dominated (median ±0.117 from a 1px ROI change), so it cannot carry a tight threshold"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 579b1254-323f-42d1-b482-42c5ad365f5c
---

Measured 2026-08-17 on `DRAGOJEVICvsHONDA.mp4`: re-OCRing the *same* scoreboard
digits under a ≤1px change to the calibrated ROI moves EasyOCR's line
confidence by a **median of 0.117, max 0.433**. 30% of correct timer readings
straddle 0.7. So `SCOREBOARD_OCR_MIN_CONFIDENCE` gates on a quantity noisier
than any increment worth tuning, and there is a feedback loop: calibration only
unions boxes clearing the floor, so changing the floor changes the ROI, which
changes the confidences again.

**Why:** it means "tune the OCR confidence threshold" is never the right
framing for a scoreboard-coverage problem — the number is not measuring
reading quality. What actually rejects bad reads is structural: the
seconds>59/minutes>59 range check in `parsers.py` and the clock-intercept fit
in `fight_segmentation.py`.

**How to apply:** to check whether a timer read is real, don't look at
confidence — compute `k = frame/fps + seconds_remaining` and test whether it
agrees with the round's intercept. Real reads cluster within ~0.5s (the 2 Hz
sampling quantum); misreads land far off. This is a label-free correctness
check and is how the 0.7→0.5 change was validated over 4781 samples with zero
false reads. See [[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]].

===== fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan.md
---
name: fight-ai-tracking-rewrite-plan
description: "Agreed 3-stage plan to replace fight-ai's hand-tuned strike/state rule cascade with a trained skeleton action model"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33d53a76-2e95-4b0d-8e5e-7581da1e9f7c
---

As of 2026-08-06, Filip and I agreed a staged plan to fix fight-ai's unreliable
punch/kick/fight-state tracking:

- **Stage 0 (in progress)** — build an eval harness before changing anything.
  Lives in `ai/eval/` (labelling tool, scorer, label-free sanity checks).
  Target ~300 labelled strikes across 2–3 fights.
- **Stage 1** — fix correctness bugs in the existing pipeline (pose→detection
  assignment collision, confidence-gate the geometry primitives, gate events to
  rounds, scale-normalise the pixel thresholds, seconds-not-frames constants).
- **Stage 2** — **chosen: train a skeleton action model** (ST-GCN / temporal CNN
  over pose sequences) to replace `detect_strikes` and `determine_fight_state`.
  Filip explicitly picked this over the alternative of a VLM-verifier-over-
  proposals approach, accepting that it is blocked on labelling first.

**Why:** the rule cascade has ~40 coupled hand-set thresholds in
`models/constants.py` and 13 commits of blind tuning with no ground truth. It
cannot be made reliable by more tuning — several constants are compensating for
bugs elsewhere rather than describing anything physical.

**How to apply:** don't propose VLM-based detection for the strike/state
problem — that fork was considered and declined. Don't change a threshold in
`constants.py` without a before/after `python -m eval.cli score` number.

===== label-events-corner-is-box-not-person.md
---
name: label-events-corner-is-box-not-person
description: "Filip labels strikes by the overlay box, not the named fighter, so label_events.corner is a track-slot pointer — the planned corner_swap flip at export would corrupt training data rather than fix it"
metadata:
  type: project
---

Stated by Filip 2026-08-31. When the overlay shows a corner swap (Roy carrying
the red box), he selects **red** and logs the punch — i.e. he picks the
rectangle around the fighter who threw it, not the fighter named red at upload.

So `label_events.corner` and `fighter_frames.corner` are **the same pointer**:
both name a track slot, not a person. Inside a `corner_swap` span they are both
"wrong" about the name and consistent about the human. The Stage 2 join
`label_events(F, corner) -> fighter_frames(F, corner) -> keypoints` therefore
already yields correct training rows with nothing applied.

**Why:** it inverts the design in the plan. Applying the swap at export — as
`ai/eval/schema.py:152` ("Applied at export time when joining labels to
fighter_frames.keypoints") and `plan/02c-labelling-ui.md:156` ("flips red/blue
in the exported training tensor") both instruct — would attach the label to the
*other* fighter's skeleton. That is the exact silent corruption
`plan/02a-upload-tracks.md:95` set out to prevent, caused by the mitigation.
The premise there was identity-labelling; the actual convention is
box-labelling, under which the corruption never existed.

**How to apply:** never apply `corner_swaps` to a label-to-keypoint join. Apply
it only where a *person* is needed (per-fighter stats, `fight_events.fighter_id`),
and at read time — mutating `fighter_frames.corner` would desync it from
`label_events.corner` and break the join that currently works. Two knock-ons:
`score.py:225`'s "fighter attribution %" is circular (the labeller read the
corner off the pipeline's own overlay, so it can never detect a swap — cf.
[[fight-ai-eval-labels-are-circular]]); and span *boundary* error no longer
corrupts training data as `plan/02d-label-quality.md:213` claims, though
detection rate still matters for the tracker metric. The spans remain the
ground truth for [[tracker-swaps-at-cuts-and-clinches]], which is now their
main purpose. See also [[corner-accuracy-blind-on-ground]].

1	# Training Lab — design brief
2	
3	> **For Claude Design.** Paste this whole file. It describes a new page for the
4	> Fight.AI web app: a dashboard over hand-labelled training data and the
5	> pipeline's measured accuracy. Every number under "Sample" is **illustrative** —
6	> realistic in shape, modelled on the fights in this repo, not a live snapshot.
7	> The visual language must match the existing app (§14).
8	
9	## 1. Context
10	
11	Fight.AI turns MMA fight video into structured events. A Python pipeline detects
12	both fighters, tracks them, estimates 17-point pose skeletons, assigns red/blue
13	corners, reads the scoreboard to find rounds, then runs a hand-tuned rule cascade
14	that emits strikes (`jab_head`, `ground_punch`, …) and fight state
15	(STRIKING / CLINCH / GROUND).
16	
17	That rule cascade is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model, which is
18	blocked on **labelled data**. A human watches a fight in the **Annotate** page and
19	logs every strike, state change, takedown, round boundary, corner swap and
20	excluded stretch. The target is **~300 labelled strikes across 2–3 fights**
21	(~10–15 min of round time) before training; ~50 is already useful for evaluation.
22	
23	A labelled fight becomes one of two things, never both:
24	
25	- **Training fight** — its labels and skeletons feed the model.
26	- **Evaluation fixture** — it is re-run through the full AI pipeline and the
27	  predictions are scored against the labels (strike precision/recall/F1, fight
28	  state, rounds).
29	
30	Today all of this lives in CLI output (`python -m eval.cli summary | score |
31	sanity`). The Training Lab puts it on one page.
32	
33	## 2. Users and the questions the page answers
34	
35	Users: 1–3 pipeline developers who label fights and change the pipeline.
36	Technical, data-literate, rightly suspicious of any unqualified number.
37	Desktop-first.
38	
39	In priority order, the page must answer:
40	
41	1. **How much labelled data do we have, of which kinds, and how far are we from
42	   the 300-strike target?**
43	2. **Is it trainable?** Which classes are starved? Is one fight dominating?
44	3. **What is the pipeline's current accuracy — and how far can that number be
45	   trusted?**
46	4. **Did the last pipeline change help or hurt?** Against the frozen baseline and
47	   the previous version.
48	5. **Is the ground truth itself healthy?** Rounds confirmed, swaps marked, no open
49	   spans, source video still on disk, exported to git.
50	6. **What should I do next?** Finish labelling X, export Y, re-run Z as a fixture,
51	   fix a failing check.
52	
53	**10-second test:** someone opening the page cold can say "213 of 300 strikes,
54	ground punches dominate, strike F1 isn't measurable yet because no labelled fight
55	has predictions."
56	
57	## 3. Honesty rules — design these in, they are the point of the page
58	
59	This project has been misled repeatedly by numbers that looked fine. Each rule
60	matches a real trap in this codebase.
61	
62	1. **Every metric shows its n and its provenance.** F1 always travels with the
63	   ground-truth strike count, the fixture count, the matching tolerance
64	   (±0.25 s = ±12 frames at 50 fps) and the pipeline version (short git SHA +
65	   constants hash). No bare percentages.
66	2. **"Not measured", "Not scorable" and "Unverified" are first-class states —
67	   never 0%, never blank.** A labelled fight processed on the manual track has no
68	   predictions: its F1 is *not scorable*, not 0%.
69	3. **Circular metrics are visibly flagged, or hidden.**
70	   - *Corner read-back* (the labeller's corner matches the pipeline's on matched
71	     strikes) reads ~100% by construction: the labeller clicks the overlay box the
72	     pipeline drew, so a tracker swap is copied into the label. Never call it
73	     "attribution accuracy". It sits behind a `Circular` badge.
74	   - *Round IoU* is circular when the labelled round spans were auto-seeded from
75	     the pipeline's own output and never edited. Show `Seeded — not verified`
76	     instead of an IoU.
77	4. **Lower bounds say so.** Corner-swap coverage (share of round time inside
78	   labeller-marked swap spans) is a *lower bound* on corner-assignment error until
79	   labeller swap recall is measured. Render it as `≥ 4.4%`.
80	5. **Low evidence is not a pass.** A label-free corner check with few decisive
81	   frames is `Unverified`, even when it reads 100%.
82	6. **Accuracy is shown against the human ceiling.** With a double-labelling
83	   agreement measurement: `F1 56.7% · human ceiling 91.4%`. Without one:
84	   `ceiling not measured`. An F1 with no ceiling can't be judged good or bad.
85	7. **Fight state leads with stability, not per-frame accuracy.** Per-frame
86	   accuracy is dominated by the most common state and stays high while the state
87	   machine visibly flaps. Lead with transitions/min and median dwell, truth vs
88	   predicted.
89	8. **Numbers are only comparable at the same tolerance and on the same fixture
90	   set.** A trend line breaks (gap plus a note) wherever either changes.
91	
92	## 4. Placement and layout
93	
94	- **Nav:** add **Lab** to the header after Analysis and Library (the app already
95	  uses "Lab Report" wording). Route `/lab`. Page title "Training Lab", subtitle
96	  "Labelled data and pipeline accuracy".
97	- **Width:** max 1440 px, centred, 22 px / 30 px page padding — same as the Player.
98	- **One scrolling page**, with a compact sticky section index on wide screens:
99	  1. Filter row
100	  2. **A** Overview
101	  3. **B** Annotated events
102	  4. **C** Spans & coverage
103	  5. **D** Fight ledger
104	  6. **E** Pipeline accuracy
105	  7. **F** Pipeline health (label-free)
106	  8. **G** Label quality & action queue
107	  - A reference drawer (taxonomy mapping, §13) opens from section B's header.
108	- **Grid:** 12 columns, 14 px gaps. Every section is a glass card (§14).
109	
110	## 5. Filter row
111	
112	One left-aligned row under the page title. It scopes everything below it.
113

# Training Lab (`/lab`) — findings and plan

> **Status: draft.** Awaiting answers on design-project access, scope, and the
> reference↔run pairing mechanism. Findings below are verified against the live
> database and working tree on 2026-09-14.

## Context

Fight.AI turns MMA video into structured events. The rule cascade that emits
strikes and fight state is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model,
and everything about that depends on measured accuracy — which today lives only
in CLI stdout (`python -m eval.cli summary | score | sanity`).

`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` (717 lines, written 10 Sep) specs a `/lab` page
for this. **No `/lab` code exists** — `grep -rniE "\blab\b|training.?lab"
frontend/src` returns nothing.

Since the brief was written, two commits changed the model it assumes:

- `fc13725` added `fights.purpose` (`training_data` | `reference` | `ai_labeled`),
  set once at upload and never changed. A fight's pipeline never re-runs.
- `9bd41d1` merged `label_events` + `label_spans` into one `fight_events` table
  with `source` / `kind` discriminators. **The brief's Appendix cites the dropped
  tables and is stale.**

The user's workflow is now: upload the bout once as `reference` and hand-label
it; then upload the *same source video* again, once per pipeline version, as
`ai_labeled`. Accuracy is a **cross-fight** comparison between two fight ids.

## Verified state of the data (2026-09-14)

```
 id |               video_path               | fps |       state       |   purpose
 60 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4    |  50 | labeling_complete | reference
 62 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4  |  50 | completed         | ai_labeled
```

Both files are 612,577,927 bytes — the same video uploaded twice. Both rows
report 43,100 frames, 50 fps, and the same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16).

| | fight 60 (reference) | fight 62 (pipeline run 1) |
|---|---|---|
| strike rows | **227 labels** (114 red / 113 blue) | **147 predictions** (78 / 69) |
| state marks | 5 (`striking` 3, `clinch` 2, **ground 0**) | **0** |
| rounds | 1025–10025 · 13900–22900 · 26525–35525 | **byte-identical** |
| `fighter_frames` | 74,083 rows, all with keypoints | **74,083**, all with keypoints |
| `corner_swap` spans | **14**, covering 11,429 of 27,000 round frames = **42.3%** | — |
| `excluded` spans | 1 (35508–35525) | — |
| round label spans | seeded from `rounds`, one shared microsecond `created_at`, **never adjusted** | auto-seeded (Annotate was opened on it) |

Ground-truth class distribution on fight 60 (top): `left_hook·head` 77,
`jab·head` 35, `cross·head` 30, `right_hook·head` 22, `low_kick` 14,
`high_kick` 14, `calf_kick` 10, `middle_kick` 9, `cross·body` 4,
`right_uppercut` 4, `clinch_knee` 3, `left_uppercut` 3, `right_hook·body` 1,
`jab·body` 1. No ground-and-pound, no elbows, no takedowns — a standing fight.

Pipeline vocabulary on fight 62: `jab_head` 25, `hook_body` 24, `low_kick` 21,
`jab_body` 20, `hook_head` 16, `cross_head` 15, `middle_kick` 14, `cross_body` 9,
`head_kick` 1, `uppercut_head` 1, `uppercut_body` 1. **No knee, no elbow, no
ground/clinch punch.**

## Blockers — no honest number can be shown until these are fixed

1. **The scorer cannot see any prediction.** `ai/eval/predictions.py:130`
   gates the strike branch on `_STRIKE_RE.match(row.description)`, but migration
   `f0a1b2c3d4e5` NULLed `description` on every non-`fight_end` point row.
   Verified: all 147 prediction rows on fight 62 have `description IS NULL` and
   `fighter_id` populated. Today `score` would report P/R/F1 = 0 — not because
   the pipeline is bad, but because nothing is loaded.
   Fix: read `action` + derive corner from `fighter_id == fights.red_fighter_id`
   (the same rule `frontend/src/utils/liveStats.ts:attributedCorner` already uses).
2. **`score.py` is single-fight.** It loads labels and predictions for one
   `video`. The new model needs labels from fight A and predictions from fight B.
3. **Nothing records which pipeline version produced a run**, and nothing links
   fight 62 back to fight 60. Today it is inferable only from the `_2` filename
   suffix and `created_at`. `ai/manifest.py` exists but is never called.
4. **No eval persistence and no HTTP surface.** `backend/app/api/routes/` has
   zero metrics endpoints; `--json` exists only on `sanity` and `score`;
   `corner_accuracy` and `corner-swap-recall` print only.
5. **Fight state is unmeasurable.** `SELECT state, count(*) FROM fight_events
   WHERE state IS NOT NULL` returns **zero rows across the entire database**.
   The pipeline has never persisted a state change.

## Changes to what the page should display

Grounded in the numbers above; each replaces or re-scopes a part of the brief.

1. **Make the run axis the spine of section E, not a footnote.** The brief's E8
   trend chart is the last item; under the new workflow it is the primary object.
   E should open with "Runs against BILANDZIC vs LUPASCU" — one row per
   `ai_labeled` fight, newest first, each with P/R/F1 and the delta vs the
   previous run. The trend line is that table plotted.
2. **Add a reference-pair provenance card**, asserting the two fights really are
   the same bout: same byte size, same `reported_frames`, same fps, same fighter
   ids. A mismatch is critical — every frame-indexed label would be misaligned.
3. **Add run-to-run determinism, independent of ground truth.** Because each run
   is a fresh pass over the identical video, a diff against the previous run is
   free and answers "did my change do anything at all?" before F1 is consulted:
   rounds identical (60/62 are), `fighter_frames` row count identical (74,083
   both), strike count 147 → next. The brief has nothing like this.
4. **Lead E3 with truth-vs-predicted counts per class, not accuracy tiles.** The
   real story here is invisible in a "target zone 71.8%" tile: the pipeline
   predicted `hook_body` 24× and `jab_body` 20× against 1 and 1 in ground truth.
   It is systematically calling body. Show the paired counts first.
5. **Compute "structurally impossible" from the run's own vocabulary.** The brief
   hardcodes elbow as `Always a miss`. Fight 62 emits no knee either, so the 3
   labelled `clinch_knee` are guaranteed FN. Derive this per run.
6. **Fight state renders `Not measured` with its reason** — "the pipeline
   persisted 0 state changes" — not an empty dumbbell chart.
7. **Corner swaps are the headline of section C, not a footnote.** 42.3% of
   labelled round time on fight 60 sits inside a marked swap, against the brief's
   illustrative `≥ 4.4%`. Per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` this does
   *not* corrupt the label→keypoint join, but it does make "corner read-back"
   worthless on this pair and per-fighter stats unreliable for 42% of the fight.
8. **Replace round IoU with `Seeded — not verified` plus cross-run agreement.**
   Fight 60's round spans are byte-identical to its own `rounds` row with a
   shared microsecond timestamp, and 62's rounds equal 60's exactly — IoU is
   100% and circular twice over. The honest signal is determinism, not accuracy.
9. **Split the training-progress hero in two.** 227 of the 300 strikes are on a
   `reference` fight, which is explicitly held out of training. One meter for
   training ground truth (`purpose='training_data'` only), one for evaluation
   ground truth (`reference`).
10. **Retire the `⚠ Both` role warning.** `purpose` makes training/eval overlap
    structurally impossible. The live risk in the new model is a video stem
    uploaded under two purposes, or a run paired to the wrong reference.

## Open questions

- Access to the Claude Design project (`f026815c…`, `Training Lab.html` + 6
  asset files) — DesignSync needs a one-time `/design-login`.
- Scope of the first implementation pass.
- How a run is tied to its reference fight.

"""Rough preview of the 60-vs-62 score: optimal 1:1 temporal matching within a
tolerance, restricted to round spans, mirroring ai/eval/score.py's contract.
Read-only; throwaway."""
import csv, sys
from itertools import product

ROUNDS = [(1025, 10025), (13900, 22900), (26525, 35525)]
EXCLUDED = [(35508, 35525)]
FPS = 50

LABEL_FAMILY = {
    "jab": "jab", "cross": "cross",
    "left_hook": "hook", "right_hook": "hook",
    "left_uppercut": "uppercut", "right_uppercut": "uppercut",
    "elbow": "elbow",
    "calf_kick": ("kick", "leg"), "low_kick": ("kick", "leg"),
    "middle_kick": ("kick", "body"), "high_kick": ("kick", "head"),
    "clinch_knee": ("knee", "unknown"), "ground_knee": ("knee", "unknown"),
    "clinch_punch": ("punch", "unknown"), "ground_punch": ("punch", "unknown"),
}
PRED_MAP = {
    "jab_head": ("jab", "head"), "jab_body": ("jab", "body"),
    "cross_head": ("cross", "head"), "cross_body": ("cross", "body"),
    "hook_head": ("hook", "head"), "hook_body": ("hook", "body"),
    "uppercut_head": ("uppercut", "head"), "uppercut_body": ("uppercut", "body"),
    "low_kick": ("kick", "leg"), "middle_kick": ("kick", "body"),
    "head_kick": ("kick", "head"),
    "clinch_knee": ("knee", "unknown"), "ground_knee": ("knee", "unknown"),
    "clinch_punch": ("punch", "unknown"), "ground_punch": ("punch", "unknown"),
}


def in_scope(f):
    if any(a <= f <= b for a, b in EXCLUDED):
        return False
    return any(a <= f <= b for a, b in ROUNDS)


def load_labels(path):
    out = []
    for frame, action, target, corner in csv.reader(open(path)):
        frame = int(frame)
        if not in_scope(frame):
            continue
        m = LABEL_FAMILY.get(action)
        if m is None:
            continue
        fam, tgt = (m, target or "unknown") if isinstance(m, str) else m
        out.append({"frame": frame, "family": fam, "target": tgt,
                    "corner": int(corner), "action": action})
    return out


def load_preds(path):
    out = []
    for frame, action, corner in csv.reader(open(path)):
        frame = int(frame)
        if not in_scope(frame):
            continue
        fam, tgt = PRED_MAP.get(action, ("punch", "unknown"))
        out.append({"frame": frame, "family": fam, "target": tgt,
                    "corner": int(corner), "action": action})
    return out


def match(gt, pr, tol):
    """Optimal 1:1 on |offset| via scipy if available, else greedy by distance."""
    pairs = [(i, j, abs(g["frame"] - p["frame"]))
             for (i, g), (j, p) in product(enumerate(gt), enumerate(pr))
             if abs(g["frame"] - p["frame"]) <= tol]
    pairs.sort(key=lambda t: t[2])
    used_g, used_p, matched = set(), set(), []
    for i, j, d in pairs:
        if i in used_g or j in used_p:
            continue
        used_g.add(i); used_p.add(j); matched.append((i, j))
    return matched


def report(gt, pr, tol):
    matched = match(gt, pr, tol)
    tp, fp, fn = len(matched), len(pr) - len(matched), len(gt) - len(matched)
    prec = tp / (tp + fp) if tp + fp else 0.0
    rec = tp / (tp + fn) if tp + fn else 0.0
    f1 = 2 * prec * rec / (prec + rec) if prec + rec else 0.0
    offsets = sorted(pr[j]["frame"] - gt[i]["frame"] for i, j in matched)
    bias = offsets[len(offsets) // 2] if offsets else 0
    jitter = sorted(abs(o - bias) for o in offsets)
    jitter = jitter[len(jitter) // 2] if jitter else 0

    spec = [(i, j) for i, j in matched if gt[i]["target"] != "unknown"

# Training Lab (`/lab`) — full-stack plan

> Findings verified against the live database and working tree on 2026-09-14.
> The Claude Design project (`f026815c…`) was **not** readable — `DesignSync`
> still reports no design-system authorization. Once `/design-login` has been run
> from a terminal, import `Training Lab.html` + the six asset files and reconcile
> "Build · 3 · Frontend" against them before any UI is written.

## Context

Fight.AI turns MMA video into structured events. The rule cascade that emits
strikes and fight state is being replaced by a trained skeleton action model,
and everything about that depends on measured accuracy — which today lives only
in CLI stdout (`python -m eval.cli summary | score | sanity`).

`frontend/TRAINING_LAB_BRIEF.md` (717 lines, written 10 Sep) specs a `/lab` page
for this. **No `/lab` code exists** — `grep -rniE "\blab\b|training.?lab"
frontend/src` returns nothing.

Since the brief was written, two commits changed the model it assumes:

- `fc13725` added `fights.purpose` (`training_data` | `reference` | `ai_labeled`),
  set once at upload and never changed. A fight's pipeline never re-runs.
- `9bd41d1` merged `label_events` + `label_spans` into one `fight_events` table
  with `source` / `kind` discriminators. **The brief's Appendix cites the dropped
  tables and is stale.**

The user's workflow is now: upload the bout once as `reference` and hand-label
it; then upload the *same source video* again, once per pipeline version, as
`ai_labeled`. Accuracy is a **cross-fight** comparison between two fight ids.

## Verified state of the data (2026-09-14)

```
 id |               video_path               | fps |       state       |   purpose
 60 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU.mp4    |  50 | labeling_complete | reference
 62 | fight_videos/BILANDZICvsLUPASCU_2.mp4  |  50 | completed         | ai_labeled
```

Both files are 612,577,927 bytes — the same video uploaded twice. Both rows
report 43,100 frames, 50 fps, and the same fighter ids (red 15, blue 16).

| | fight 60 (reference) | fight 62 (pipeline run 1) |
|---|---|---|
| strike rows | **227 labels** (114 red / 113 blue) | **147 predictions** (78 / 69) |
| state marks | 5 (`striking` 3, `clinch` 2, **ground 0**) | **0** |
| rounds | 1025–10025 · 13900–22900 · 26525–35525 | **byte-identical** |
| `fighter_frames` | 74,083 rows, all with keypoints | **74,083**, all with keypoints |
| `corner_swap` spans | **14**, covering 11,429 of 27,000 round frames = **42.3%** | — |
| `excluded` spans | 1 (35508–35525) | — |
| round label spans | seeded from `rounds`, one shared microsecond `created_at`, **never adjusted** | auto-seeded (Annotate was opened on it) |

Ground-truth class distribution on fight 60 (top): `left_hook·head` 77,
`jab·head` 35, `cross·head` 30, `right_hook·head` 22, `low_kick` 14,
`high_kick` 14, `calf_kick` 10, `middle_kick` 9, `cross·body` 4,
`right_uppercut` 4, `clinch_knee` 3, `left_uppercut` 3, `right_hook·body` 1,
`jab·body` 1. No ground-and-pound, no elbows, no takedowns — a standing fight.

Pipeline vocabulary on fight 62: `jab_head` 25, `hook_body` 24, `low_kick` 21,
`jab_body` 20, `hook_head` 16, `cross_head` 15, `middle_kick` 14, `cross_body` 9,
`head_kick` 1, `uppercut_head` 1, `uppercut_body` 1. **No knee, no elbow, no
ground/clinch punch.**

## The training set is no longer volume-limited — the brief's hero is stale

`purpose='training_data'` across 5 fights now holds **800 labelled strikes**, not
the brief's 213. The 300-strike target is met at 267%. What is wrong with the set
is its shape:

| Training family | Examples | Note |
|---|---|---|
| jab | 245 | |
| hook | 196 | |
| punch (ground + clinch) | 130 | 119 of them from one fight |
| cross | 93 | |
| knee | 40 | |
| kick | 29 | `calf_kick` 2 · `low_kick` 3 — far below any minimum |
| uppercut | 24 | at the brief's default minimum of 25 |
| **elbow** | **0** | no examples at all |

And fight 54 (VITASOVIC vs STOSIC) holds **538 of 800 = 67%** — the brief's
"largest-fight share, warning above 50%" tile, live and failing.

So the hero card should stop counting toward 300 and start showing what actually
blocks training: **classes below the minimum, and single-fight dominance.** Keep
the 300 counter as a small stat tile for history.

## Preview of the number the page will show

I reimplemented the scorer's contract approximately (1:1 temporal matching,
in-round only, minus the excluded span) over the real rows, to know what the page
has to render. **Approximate** — greedy-nearest instead of the Hungarian
assignment `score.py` uses, and my own label→family map — so the real scorer will
shift these a little.

```
±12 f (0.24 s)   TP 84  FP 63  FN 143   P 57.1%  R 37.0%  F1 44.9%
±25 f (0.50 s)   TP 98  FP 49  FN 129   P 66.7%  R 43.2%  F1 52.4%
±50 f (1.00 s)   identical to ±25 — nothing further is within reach
bias −1 f (−20 ms) · jitter 2 f
family 54.2% (n=83) · target 61.4% (n=83) · corner read-back 75.0% (n=84)
```

Two things fall out of this immediately:

- **Timing is not the problem.** Bias −1 frame, jitter 2 frames, and F1 plateaus
  by ±25 f. The tolerance debate in `plan/02d-label-quality.md` is moot for this
  pair; the pipeline simply misses 129 of 227 strikes.
- **The class-count table is the finding, and no accuracy tile would show it:**

| family · target | truth | predicted |
|---|---|---|
| hook · head | **99** | **16** |
| hook · body | **1** | **24** |
| jab · head | 35 | 25 |
| jab · body | **1** | **20** |
| cross · head | 30 | 15 |
| cross · body | 4 | 9 |
| kick · leg | 24 | 21 |
| kick · body | 9 | 14 |
| kick · head | **14** | **1** |
| uppercut · head | 7 | 1 |
| knee | 3 | **0** |

  The target classifier is biased hard toward `body`, and head hooks — the single
  most common strike in the fight, 99 of 227 — are detected 16 times. That is the
  actionable number, and the brief's E3 ("Target zone 71.8%") would bury it.

### The cross-fight model turns corner read-back into a real metric — and it fails

The brief hides corner read-back behind a `Circular` badge because the labeller
clicks the same pipeline's overlay, so a tracker swap is copied into the label
and cancels out. **That reasoning does not hold across two fights.** The labels
were read off fight 60's overlay; the predictions carry fight 62's independent
`fighter_id`. Nothing cancels.

89 of the 227 labels (39%) fall inside one of fight 60's 14 `corner_swap` spans,
so per `label-events-corner-is-box-not-person` the stored `corner` is a track
slot and must be resolved to a person — at read time, by flipping inside a swap
span — before it can be compared with fight 62's `fighter_id`:

```
raw slot vs person     63/84 = 75.0%
swap-resolved          45/84 = 53.6%     ← chance, on a two-way choice
```

Fight 62 has no swap spans marked, so its `fighter_id` carries whatever swaps its
own tracker made. **That makes 53.6% genuine fighter-attribution accuracy for the
run, and it is at chance.** It is the first time this project has been able to
measure that number at all, and it deserves a tile in section E rather than a
collapsed row with a `Circular` badge.

Caveat: my matching is approximate, so some of the 84 pairs may be spurious;
treat 53.6% as "at or near chance", not as a precise figure, until the real
scorer runs.

1. **The scorer cannot see any prediction.** `ai/eval/predictions.py:130`

   `fighter_id` populated. Today `score` would report P/R/F1 = 0 — not because
   the pipeline is bad, but because nothing is loaded.

2. **`score.py` is single-fight.** It loads labels and predictions for one
   `video`. The new model needs labels from fight A and predictions from fight B.
3. **Nothing records which pipeline version produced a run**, and nothing links

[PASS] no simultaneous mutual strikes  0 frames … (0/0 events)

[FAIL] strike rate is plausible        0 in-round strikes over 9.0 min = 0.0/min

[PASS] round count fits video length

## 1. The new table

### Recommendation: one table, `eval_runs`, cached report as **JSONB in the row**

**Grain:** one row per *measured fight* (`run_fight_id`), `UNIQUE`. Because a fight's pipeline never re-runs, "fight" and "pipeline version" are 1:1 for scored runs — the trend line's x-axis is a sequence of different `ai_labeled` fight ids over the same reference. Re-scoring is an `UPDATE` in place (a score at a different tolerance isn't comparable to the one it replaces anyway).

**`reference_fight_id` is nullable.** A row with it NULL is a label-free measurement of one fight (sanity + corner accuracy only) — that's what serves brief §F for fights 42/44/58 that have no reference pair. A row with it set is a scored fixture (§E). One table, one row = one fight's complete measurement record.

**JSONB, not `ai/eval/reports/`.** Four reasons:
1. The backend cannot reach `ai/`'s filesystem conventions cleanly — it runs in a different venv with `AI_DIR` as an env override, and would need a whole path-resolution + file-serving layer mirroring `_resolve_video_path`.
2. Atomicity. The comparability keys (`tolerance_secs`, `reference_fight_id`, `git_sha`) live in columns *beside* the blob, so a SQL query can refuse a comparison without parsing JSON, and the row can never disagree with the file it points at.
3. The trend query is one statement: `SELECT scored_at, score_report->'strikes'->'detection' FROM eval_runs WHERE reference_fight_id = :r AND tolerance_secs = :t ORDER BY scored_at` — no fan-out of file reads, and pooled TP/FP/FN is `SUM((score_report->'strikes'->'detection'->>'tp')::int)`.
4. Size is trivial: the unbounded parts are `missed`/`spurious`, bounded here at 227 + 147 entries.

Keep `report_io.save_report(path)` and the `--json` flag exactly as they are — `ai/eval/baselines/*.json` stays the git-committed artifact. `report_path` records where that copy went, so the ledger can show "exported". JSONB is the dashboard's source of truth; disk is the archive. Not either/or.

**Rejected alternative:** splitting into `eval_runs` (pairing) + `eval_reports` (blobs, one per kind). ### The live-vs-cached boundary

**The backend must never import `ai/eval`.** It runs in a separate venv (`pipeline_runner.AI_PYTHON`), and `score.py` pulls numpy + scipy, `corner_accuracy.py` pulls cv2, and everything under `eval/` imports `ai/database.py`'s own `SessionLocal`. `pipeline_runner.py` already establishes the boundary: cross-venv work is a subprocess that writes JSON.

That draws the line cleanly:

- **Live SQL** — anything expressible over `fights` / `fight_events` / `rounds` / `fighter_frames`: sections A, B, C, D, G2 and the tolerance ceiling in G1.
- **Cached (`eval_runs` JSONB)** — anything that needs `ai/eval` code to run: score (E), sanity (F1), corner accuracy (F2), agreement ceiling and swap recall (G1).

Every live query must carry an explicit `source`/`kind` filter — `backend/CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule for `fight_events`, and the one most likely to be broken by a new aggregate.
